task: Fix seven rendering and interaction defects in LLM-generated A2UI interactive surfaces (typography, read-only affordance, narrow-width containment, shared-conversation guard, checkbox/label alignment, checkbox/radio design-system parity, filterable-picker spacing).

component_scope.label: L
component_scope.affected: src/a2ui/theme.css (surface stylesheet, ~150 added lines), src/a2ui/renderers.tsx (ButtonRenderer class list), ChatA2uiBlock.tsx (isSurfaceActive predicate + useChatContext read), new shared test helper src/a2ui/__tests__/themeCssRules.ts

requirements_clarity.label: L
requirements_clarity.gaps: AC-1 ('renders correctly') and AC-2 ('usable and accessible') are unfalsifiable as written and closed only 'partial' in review. CR-006 (button label clipping vs wrapping) was triaged decision_needed and escalated to a human mid-implementation, causing a clip -> wrap -> break-all rework. AC-5 carries a deliberate behavioural asymmetry (unanswered last-turn surface now locked in the shared view) still flagged for confirmation with the ticket author. AC-6 (Edge verification) remains formally unmet.

technical_risk.label: L
technical_risk.risk_factors: No precedent for the approach: the published @a2ui/react build ships empty CSS-module class maps, so elements render class="undefined" and the SDK sets border/background/outline via inline style. Fixes therefore rest on structural selectors, specificity arithmetic and targeted !important rather than utility classes. The change introduced a critical accessibility regression of its own (appearance:none removed the UA focus ring while the SDK's inline outline:none defeated the replacement), plus two self-inflicted visual regressions found during the work (appearance:none collapsing bare picker options to 0x0; wrong accent token rendering a checked control white-on-white in the dark theme). Selectors match on serialised inline-style substrings, which over-matched the catalog's horizontal List scroller. Engine-sensitive features (:has(), appearance:none with ::after glyphs) verified in Chrome only. jsdom computes no layout, so no test can observe the cascade.
technical_risk.mitigation: Every selector is prefixed .a2ui-scope, which mounts in exactly one place, so blast radius is bounded to a2ui surfaces. Pure CSS plus one boolean predicate — trivially revertible. One full code-review round (13 findings, 1 critical) plus a check round (1 further finding) all resolved and mutation-tested; live browser measurement used as the acceptance evidence in place of unit assertions.

file_change_estimate.label: XL
file_change_estimate.note: The raw diffstat (21 files, 2726 insertions) overstates code volume: 7 files and roughly 1500 lines are planning/review artefacts under docs/superpowers/. Production source is 3 files (~150 CSS lines plus two one-line component edits). Scored XL on the source-only surface of 14 files with 9 new test files across 2 source directories, not on the raw 21.

key_reasoning.reason: 14 source files touched — 3 production, 11 test — with 9 new test files across 2 directories. Production code itself is small (theme.css +~150 lines, one className on ButtonRenderer, one import/hook/condition in ChatA2uiBlock), but the test surface was rebuilt: five suites were rewritten onto a new themeCssRules helper after review found the original regex greps passed against the exact regressions they claimed to catch.

Seven independent defects, each fixed at its own layer, plus design-system parity work reproducing Checkbox.tsx and RadioButton.tsx appearance in raw CSS. theme.css is shared by every a2ui surface, so each rule is cross-cutting within the subsystem — evidenced by review findings CR-002, CR-004, CR-010 and CR-012, all cases of a new rule reaching markup it was not reasoning about.

Difficulty was concentrated in cascade reasoning against third-party SDK markup that ships empty CSS-module class maps and sets properties inline — specificity and !important arithmetic mattered more than volume. The change introduced a critical keyboard-focus regression of its own and two self-inflicted visual regressions during the work; jsdom computes no layout so nothing could be proven by unit test, and cross-browser (Edge) verification remains unmet.

Two acceptance criteria are unfalsifiable as written and closed 'partial'; one finding (button-label truncation) was a genuine product trade-off escalated to a human and reworked twice before landing on break-all + max-w-full; one behavioural asymmetry in the shared view still needs author confirmation.

red_flags_applied: Requirements Clarity bumped from M (3) to L (4): vague acceptance criteria — AC-1 'renders correctly' and AC-2 'usable and accessible' carry no measurable threshold and both closed 'partial' in review.
